data.body: The pre-commit ruff (check + format) keeps regressing because merges land before the ruff-format is clean at the merge point, so a git push on the primary fails. Make ruff a merge-enforced concern: default/configure [ci].command to run `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` before merge and auto-fix (ruff check --fix / ruff format) with the corrections recorded, so a changed file cannot merge with lint drift. Regression test: a branch with ruff drift is refused/auto-corrected by the ci gate before merge.
data.title: make ruff check+format a merge-enforced ci gate (auto-fix) per project: add ruff to [ci].command before merge, with correction of any issues it finds

data.claim: superseded_by with no paths falls back to ancestry alone and returns True for ANY descendant commit, including one touching only .ddflow/events; the fix makes the no-paths case read the diff and supersede only when a non-bookkeeping source file changed.
data.falsifier: A phase-scoped superseded_by call (paths=None) over a commit that changed only .ddflow/events must return False; the regression test that would refute the fix asserts not superseded_by(began, now, cwd) for an event-only commit.
data.mechanism: evidence.py superseded_by: when  is empty it returns True before asking git which files changed; a phase item has no globs, so  is None and even a .ddflow/events-only commit advances ancestry and supersedes the run.
data.probe_output: FAILED on unfixed code: AssertionError: assert not True (event-only commit superseded). PASSED after the fix (5 passed with test_gate_supersede_content.py).
data.question: Does superseded_by treat an event-only commit as superseding a phase gate run (which has no globs)?

chunk_findings.detail: `spent` is snapshotted from the first process (`spent = p.elapsed_s`) before the selected-run stage loop, and both the early return and the final `return p, before, spent` hand that same value back. The comment says it is summed across stages, but a selected run whose selection passes and then runs `always_command` (or the guard stages that rebind `p`) never adds those stages' wall time. Given a selection that finishes in 2.0s and an always stage that runs 30s, the recorded `elapsed_s` is 2.0, so `ddflow metrics` still times only part of the finished run — the bias B28537b615d is meant to remove for selected and partial outcomes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/runner.py:_execute

chunk_findings.detail: `gate_untimed` counts RAN outcomes with no `gate.started` and no `elapsed_s`, but that dict is only copied onto rows built from `per_gate` (`for g, v in sorted(per_gate.items())`). `per_gate` is filled only from `gate_durations`, which drops exactly those outcomes. Given a view whose only ci outcomes are untimed (one `gate.passed` with empty evidence, `min_samples` 1), `gate_untimed` is `{"ci": 1}` and `gate_time` is `[]`, so the count is discarded and ci is still a silent omission — the case the bug is about when a window has no timed sibling. The new test always adds a timed `elapsed_s: 50` row, so it never fails this input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/summary.py:gate_time

chunk_findings.detail: The regression only asserts `"elapsed_s" in ev and ev["elapsed_s"] >= 0`. A finished `ddflow ci run` that stamps `elapsed_s=0` (or any constant) passes, so it does not show the recorded value is that run’s command time. The expected fix also required the outcome to carry `waited_s` and not double-record a later run on the same tree; this test checks neither, so those failures stay green.
